Question_Text: How does a person with good posture usually feel?
Hint: Body systems work better.
Detailed_Solution: Efficiency of organs leads to feeling more energetic.

Question_Text: Proper posture ensures that ______ and bones grow well?
Hint: Muscles work with bones.
Detailed_Solution: The muscular and skeletal systems both benefit from correct body alignment.

Question_Text: Why is it harder to correct posture in adults than in children?
Hint: Think of dry clay vs wet clay.
Detailed_Solution: Children's bones are more flexible and still growing, making correction easier.

Question_Text: Good posture is a ______ habit that everyone should learn?
Hint: It benefits your whole life.
Detailed_Solution: Maintaining good posture is a fundamental healthy habit for physical well-being.

Question_Text: What is a fracture?
Hint: Think about what happens when a bone snaps.
Detailed_Solution: A fracture is defined as a cracked or broken bone in the body.

Question_Text: Which type of fracture involves a bone breaking but remaining inside the flesh?
Hint: It is also called a 'closed' fracture.
Detailed_Solution: A simple fracture occurs when the bone breaks but the skin is not pierced.

Question_Text: What defines a compound fracture?
Option_A: The bone is broken into many pieces
Option_B: The bone breaks and comes out through the skin
Hint: It is an 'open' fracture.
Detailed_Solution: A compound fracture is when the broken bone tears the flesh and is visible outside.

Question_Text: Which fracture is most common in young children because their bones are soft?
Hint: Think of a young, flexible tree branch.
Detailed_Solution: A greenstick fracture is when the bone bends and cracks but does not break completely.

Question_Text: What happens in a comminuted fracture?
Option_A: The bone breaks into several parts
Option_D: It only happens in the skull
Hint: Think of a bone being shattered.
Detailed_Solution: A comminuted fracture is a type of injury where the bone is broken into several pieces.

Question_Text: What is a sprain?
Hint: This injury happens at the joint.

Question_Text: What is a strain?
Option_D: A disease caused by a virus
Hint: Think of 'straining' your muscles.
Detailed_Solution: A strain is an injury specifically to a muscle or its tendon.

Question_Text: What occurs during a dislocation?
Option_B: Bones forming a joint are displaced from their normal position
Hint: The bones 'pop out' of the joint.
Detailed_Solution: Dislocation is the displacement of bones at a joint.

Question_Text: What is the first thing you should do when giving first aid for a fracture?
Option_B: Remove any object that caused the fracture and stop bleeding
Hint: Safety and stopping blood loss come first.
Detailed_Solution: Initial first aid involves removing hazards and controlling any bleeding.

Question_Text: What is the purpose of a splint in first aid?
Option_B: To keep the broken bones in position and prevent movement
Option_C: To make the bone grow faster
Option_D: To stop the person from crying
Hint: It acts as a temporary support.
Detailed_Solution: A splint is used to immobilize a fractured limb to prevent further injury.

Question_Text: What should be used to support a broken arm?
Option_B: An arm sling tied around the neck
Hint: It hangs from the neck.
Detailed_Solution: An arm sling is used to support and rest a broken arm.

Question_Text: What does the acronym RICE stand for in treating dislocations or sprains?

Question_Text: Which of these is a sign of a fracture?

Question_Text: If a limb appears 'crooked' or 'shortened' after a fall, it is likely a?

Detailed_Solution: Deformity or shortening of a limb is a common sign of a bone break.

Question_Text: Why should you avoid tampering with a dislocated joint?
Option_A: It might make the person laugh
Option_B: It can cause further damage to nerves and blood vessels
Hint: Only a doctor should put a bone back.
Detailed_Solution: Tampering can worsen the injury; professional medical help is required.

Question_Text: What is used to keep a fractured bone from moving further?
Hint: It is a stiff support.

Question_Text: Knock-knees and bow legs are examples of?

Detailed_Solution: These are disorders where the legs grow in curved or bent shapes.

Question_Text: What is the main difference between a sprain and a strain?

Hint: Think 'Ligament = Sprain'.

Question_Text: Sudden swelling and bruising at a joint after a twist usually indicates?

Question_Text: In case of a compound fracture, why are antiseptics used?

Question_Text: What is a club foot?

Hint: It is a skeletal disorder.

Question_Text: Which tool is used to carry a person with a broken leg to the hospital?

Detailed_Solution: A stretcher is the safest way to transport a victim with a major fracture.

Question_Text: 'Elevation' in the RICE method helps to?
Hint: Lifting the limb above the heart.
Detailed_Solution: Elevating the injured part helps drain fluid and reduce swelling.

Question_Text: A person with 'bow legs' has legs that curve?
Hint: Think of the shape of a bow.
Detailed_Solution: Bow legs curve outward at the knees.

Question_Text: Which first aid equipment is tied around the neck to support a broken wrist?

Detailed_Solution: An arm sling provides rest and support for wrist or arm injuries.

Question_Text: What is a sign of a compound fracture that you won't see in a simple fracture?

Detailed_Solution: Only compound fractures involve an open wound with visible bone.

Question_Text: To 'compress' an injury means to?
Hint: Applying pressure.
Detailed_Solution: Compression involves using a bandage to provide support and limit swelling.

Question_Text: Why is ice applied to a sprained ankle?

Question_Text: Which of these is a skeletal disorder?

Question_Text: What is the first aid for a strain (muscle injury)?
Option_B: Apply a cold compress or ice pack
Hint: Cold helps soothe muscles.
Detailed_Solution: Applying ice helps treat the pain of a torn or overstretched muscle.

Question_Text: How can you identify a dislocation without an X-ray?

Detailed_Solution: A dislocated joint will appear visibly deformed compared to the normal side.

Question_Text: If someone breaks a leg, you should ______?

Option_B: Keep them still and call for help
Option_D: Cover the whole body in salt
Hint: Immobilization is key.
Detailed_Solution: Movement can make a fracture worse; keep the patient still.

Question_Text: A 'grating' or 'grinding' sound when moving a limb after a fall suggests?

Question_Text: Why is it important to 'give comfort and assurance' to an injured person?
Option_B: To help reduce shock and keep them calm
Option_C: To make the bone heal instantly
Hint: Mental state affects physical recovery.
Detailed_Solution: Calming the victim is a vital part of first aid to prevent shock.

Question_Text: Which professional should treat all skeletal injuries?
Hint: They are trained in medicine.
Detailed_Solution: Always seek medical attention from a doctor for bone or joint injuries.

Question_Text: What is the common name for the displacement of bones at a joint?
Hint: The bones are 'dis-located'.
Detailed_Solution: Dislocation occurs when bones are forced out of their natural socket.

Question_Text: In the RICE method, what does 'C' stand for?
Hint: Using a bandage for pressure.
Detailed_Solution: Compression helps limit internal bleeding and swelling.

Question_Text: Can you see the bone in a simple fracture?
Hint: The skin remains intact.
Detailed_Solution: In a simple (closed) fracture, the bone stays inside the body.

Question_Text: A 'torn ligament' is another name for a?
Hint: Affects the joint connector.
Detailed_Solution: A sprain is specifically an injury to the ligaments.

Question_Text: What should you do before applying a splint to a compound fracture?
Option_B: Stop the bleeding and cover the wound
Hint: Wound care first.
Detailed_Solution: Open wounds must be managed before immobilizing the limb.

Question_Text: A fracture where the bone is shattered into many bits is ______?

Detailed_Solution: Comminuted fractures involve the bone breaking into several parts.

Question_Text: What is the use of crutches?
Option_A: To help an injured person move
Hint: Support for walking.

Question_Text: Why are greenstick fractures common in children?

Question_Text: What is the best way to carry a patient with a spinal injury?

Question_Text: Muscle cramps are considered a ______ system disorder?

Question_Text: What is a likely result of not immobilizing a fracture?

Question_Text: What does 'Elevate' mean in the treatment of a sprain?

Question_Text: Dislocation is common in which parts of the body?

Question_Text: In case of a sprained wrist, what is applied for support?

Question_Text: What happens when a bone is displaced?

Question_Text: Which of these symptoms is shared by fractures, sprains, and dislocations?

Question_Text: What does 'Rest' in RICE help achieve?

Question_Text: Which type of fracture involves a shattered bone?

Question_Text: Tying an arm sling around the neck provides ______ for a broken arm?

Question_Text: What should you NOT do when someone has a compound fracture?

Option_C: Cover the wound with a clean cloth
Hint: This is very dangerous.

Question_Text: Bruising is a sign of?

Question_Text: Which type of fracture is also called an 'Open Fracture'?

Question_Text: How does ice help a dislocated joint?

Question_Text: Which of these is the correct first aid tool for a leg break?

Question_Text: What is the cause of Rickets in children?
Option_B: Lack of Vitamin D and Calcium
Hint: Think about a nutrient deficiency.
Detailed_Solution: Rickets is a deficiency disease caused by a lack of Vitamin D, Calcium, or Phosphorus.

Question_Text: Which disease is caused by bacteria and leads to loss of feeling in the skin?
Hint: It also causes shortening of fingers and toes.
Detailed_Solution: Leprosy is a bacterial disease that affects the skin, nerves, and bones.

Question_Text: How is Polio spread from one person to another?
Hint: Think about hygiene and germs.
Detailed_Solution: Polio germs are spread through drinking water contaminated with infected faeces.

Question_Text: A child with 'bowlegs' is likely suffering from which disease?
Hint: This disease makes bones weak and soft.
Detailed_Solution: Rickets causes leg bones to grow in curved shapes like bowlegs or knock-knees.

Question_Text: Which vaccine is given to children to prevent Polio?
Hint: The name of the vaccine matches the disease.
Detailed_Solution: Children are immunized against Polio using the polio vaccine (usually drops in the mouth).

Question_Text: Tuberculosis of the spine is caused by a bacterium called?
Hint: It shares a name with the lung disease.
Detailed_Solution: TB of the bones/spine is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

Question_Text: What is a common sign of Tuberculosis of the spine?
Option_B: A lump growing on the spine
Hint: It affects the backbone's shape.
Detailed_Solution: A physical lump on the back and persistent backache are signs of spinal TB.

Question_Text: Which disease is caused by bacteria found in the soil entering through cuts?
Hint: It makes muscles very stiff.
Detailed_Solution: Tetanus bacteria (Clostridium tetani) live in the soil and enter via open wounds.

Question_Text: Which vaccine prevents Tetanus?
Hint: It is a triple vaccine.
Detailed_Solution: The DPT (Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus) vaccine protects against Tetanus.

Question_Text: Which disease causes a person to lose feeling in parts of their skin?
Hint: It is an infectious bacterial disease.
Detailed_Solution: A key symptom of Leprosy is the loss of sensation in the skin.

Question_Text: How can TB of the bones be spread to humans from animals?
Option_B: By drinking unboiled milk from an infected cow
Hint: Milk must be boiled or pasteurized.
Detailed_Solution: TB bacteria can be found in the milk of infected cows.

Question_Text: What is the adult version of Rickets called?
Hint: It starts with 'Osteo'.
Detailed_Solution: Osteomalacia is the lack of Vitamin D and calcium in adults, leading to fragile bones.

Question_Text: Which disease is characterized by 'stiff muscles all over the body'?
Hint: It is caused by germs in wounds.
Detailed_Solution: Tetanus causes painful muscle spasms and stiffness (lockjaw).

Question_Text: To prevent Polio, we should always drink ______ water?
Hint: Boiling kills the virus.
Detailed_Solution: Boiling water is a primary way to prevent the spread of water-borne polio germs.

Question_Text: Which mineral deficiency leads to poor teeth formation and weak bones?
Hint: Found in milk and fish.
Detailed_Solution: Calcium and phosphorus are essential for building strong bone tissue.

Question_Text: The BCG vaccine is given to prevent which disease?
Hint: It is given on the right upper arm at birth.
Detailed_Solution: BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guérin) is the vaccine for Tuberculosis.

Question_Text: What is the scientific name for the bacteria that cause Tetanus?
Hint: Look at the name carefully.
Detailed_Solution: Tetanus is caused by Clostridium tetani.

Question_Text: Which disease causes the shortening of fingers and toes if not treated?
Hint: It affects the extremities of the body.
Detailed_Solution: Leprosy can cause physical deformities like shortened fingers.

Question_Text: Why is Polio called a disease of the limbs?
Option_A: Because it only affects the arms
Option_B: Because it weakens or paralyses leg muscles
Option_C: Because it makes limbs grow longer
Hint: Paralysis leads to lameness.
Detailed_Solution: Polio virus attacks nerves, leading to muscle weakness or paralysis in the limbs.

Question_Text: Which disease is an inherited condition where voluntary muscles progressively weaken?
Hint: Check the P.7 Tekule notes page 18.
Detailed_Solution: Muscular dystrophy is a group of inherited diseases that weaken muscles.

Question_Text: Inflammation, pain, and stiffness of the joints is called?
Hint: Common in older people or after injury.
Detailed_Solution: Arthritis is the disease characterized by painful and stiff joints.

Question_Text: Which disease is caused by thinning of bones due to hormone imbalance, especially in women?
Hint: Bones become very brittle.
Detailed_Solution: Osteoporosis involves a loss of bone mineral density and tissue.

Question_Text: A person with Rickets should eat more foods rich in?
Hint: These nutrients fix the deficiency.
Detailed_Solution: Vitamin D from sun/food and calcium from milk are the cure/prevention.

Question_Text: What is a symptom of Leprosy affecting the skin?
Hint: The nerves in the skin are damaged.
Detailed_Solution: A major sign of leprosy is the loss of sensation in skin patches.

Question_Text: What is 'Osteoarthritis' primarily caused by?
Option_C: Daily wear and tear of the joint
Hint: It happens over time as we age.
Detailed_Solution: Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease from long-term use and injury.

Question_Text: Bone cancer is characterized by what?
Hint: This is how all cancers work.
Detailed_Solution: Cancer of the bones involves the uncontrolled multiplication of bone cells.

Question_Text: Why is it important to use latrines to prevent Polio?
Option_B: To prevent infected faeces from contaminating water
Hint: Proper waste disposal stops the virus.
Detailed_Solution: Polio is spread through the faecal-oral route; latrines keep germs away from water.

Question_Text: Scurvy is caused by a lack of which vitamin?
Hint: Found in citrus fruits like oranges.
Detailed_Solution: A lack of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) causes scurvy, affecting connective tissues.

Question_Text: In newborn babies, Tetanus germs can enter through which part?
Option_B: The umbilical cord if cut with dirty tools
Hint: Think about the birth process.
Detailed_Solution: Dirty instruments used on the umbilical cord can introduce Tetanus bacteria.

Question_Text: Which disease is also known as Poliomyelitis?
Hint: It is the full scientific name.
Detailed_Solution: Polio is the short name for Poliomyelitis.

Question_Text: How can we prevent Leprosy from spreading in a home?
Option_B: By not sharing towels or beddings with an infected person
Hint: It spreads through direct contact.
Detailed_Solution: Avoiding direct skin contact and sharing personal items prevents transmission.

Question_Text: Who first discovered the bacterium that causes Tuberculosis in 1882?
Hint: Check the P.7 Science notes page 15.
Detailed_Solution: Robert Koch is the scientist who identified the TB bacterium.

Question_Text: What happens to bones in a person with Rickets?
Hint: This is why they curve.
Detailed_Solution: Low calcium/Vitamin D makes bones too soft to support weight properly.

Question_Text: DPT vaccine is given on which part of a child's body?
Hint: Check the Tetanus section of the notes.
Detailed_Solution: Early immunization with DPT is given on the left upper thigh.

Question_Text: Which disease causes a baby to stop suckling its mother's breasts?
Hint: Stiff jaw muscles are the cause.
Detailed_Solution: Tetanus causes muscle spasms that prevent the baby from suckling.

Question_Text: What is a 'non-paralytic' type of Polio?
Option_A: A type that causes no pain
Option_B: A type that does not lead to permanent paralysis
Option_D: A type that affects only the brain
Hint: Check the Polio section on page 23.
Detailed_Solution: Non-paralytic polio has mild symptoms like fever and headache but no paralysis.

Question_Text: Which of these is a sign of TB of the bones?
Hint: Think about where the spine is.
Detailed_Solution: Spinal TB causes chronic back pain and difficulty walking.

Question_Text: Can Leprosy be treated?
Hint: Modern medicine can cure it.
Detailed_Solution: Early cases of leprosy are treated and cured with specific antibiotics.

Question_Text: Which disease is autoimmune in nature, where the body destroys its own joint cells?
Hint: Check the Arthritis section in the Tekule notes.
Detailed_Solution: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition.

Question_Text: What causes lameness in Polio victims?
Hint: The muscles lose their power to move.
Detailed_Solution: Polio virus destroys nerves, causing muscles to become paralyzed.

Question_Text: Which of these is a symptom of Rickets?
Hint: Think of leg deformities.
Detailed_Solution: Knock-knees and bowlegs are the primary signs of Rickets.

Question_Text: Why should milk be pasteurized to prevent TB?
Hint: Heat destroys the bacteria.
Detailed_Solution: Pasteurization kills the TB bacteria that might be present in raw cow's milk.

Question_Text: Spasms when touched is a sign of?
Hint: Involuntary muscle contractions.
Detailed_Solution: Tetanus makes the nervous system hypersensitive, causing spasms.

Question_Text: What is the effect of Leprosy on the skin?
Hint: Nerve damage is involved.
Detailed_Solution: Leprosy causes skin patches that lose sensation and change color.

Question_Text: Which disease causes 'fragile' bones that break easily in adults?
Hint: Think of the adult version of Rickets.
Detailed_Solution: Osteomalacia makes bones fragile due to low mineral content.

Question_Text: Is Polio a communicable or non-communicable disease?
Hint: It can be passed from person to person.
Detailed_Solution: Polio is an infectious/communicable disease caused by a virus.

Question_Text: The deformity of 'Kyphosis' (hunchback) can be a result of?
Hint: A lump grows on the spine.
Detailed_Solution: Spinal TB can lead to a hunchback shape as vertebrae are damaged.

Question_Text: What is the main way to prevent Tetanus in the community?
Option_B: By covering open wounds and getting vaccinated
Hint: Stop the germ from entering the body.
Detailed_Solution: Vaccination and proper wound care are the best defenses.

Question_Text: Which condition is common in women after menopause?
Hint: Check the notes on page 24.
Detailed_Solution: Hormone changes after menopause increase the risk of Osteoporosis.

Question_Text: Can Vitamin D be obtained from sunlight?
Hint: It's the sunshine vitamin.
Detailed_Solution: The body manufactures Vitamin D when skin is exposed to sunlight.

Question_Text: Which disease makes it difficult to walk because of pain in the backbone?
Hint: It targets the axial skeleton.
Detailed_Solution: Tuberculosis of the spine causes severe pain during movement.

Question_Text: The process of isolating an infected person to prevent the spread of disease is used for?
Hint: These are highly infectious diseases.
Detailed_Solution: Isolating patients with Leprosy or TB helps stop the cycle of infection.

Question_Text: Which of these is NOT a disease of the musculo-skeletal system?
Hint: Malaria is a blood disease caused by parasites.
Detailed_Solution: Malaria does not primarily target bones or muscles.

Question_Text: Why should we wash hands with soap before eating to prevent Polio?
Option_B: To kill any polio virus picked up from the environment
Hint: Hands carry germs to the mouth.
Detailed_Solution: Hygiene is key to preventing the faecal-oral transmission of Polio.

Question_Text: Which disease can be spread through 'droplet infection' in the air?
Hint: Think of coughing and sneezing.
Detailed_Solution: TB bacteria are expelled into the air by an infected person.

Question_Text: Which part of the body does Arthritis mainly affect?
Hint: It causes stiffness and swelling there.
Detailed_Solution: Arthritis is a condition specifically targeting the joints.

Question_Text: What is the consequence of untreated Polio in a child?
Hint: Paralysis leads to permanent disability.
Detailed_Solution: Muscle atrophy (wasting) and lameness are permanent effects of paralytic polio.

Question_Text: Vegetables like broccoli and fish like salmon help prevent which condition?
Hint: These are sources of calcium.
Detailed_Solution: Eating calcium-rich foods keeps the skeletal system strong.

Question_Text: Health habits like regular physical exercise help to prevent ______?
Hint: Exercise strengthens the whole system.
Detailed_Solution: Regular activity and good diet are the best ways to keep bones and muscles healthy.

  • Simple (Closed) Fracture: Bone breaks but stays inside the skin.
  • Compound (Open) Fracture: Bone breaks and tears through the skin.

Cause: A Virus.

Cause: Deficiency (lack) of Vitamin D, Calcium, and Phosphorus.

Signs: Bow-legs (bending of legs), knock-knees, and weak bones.

Prevention: Eat foods rich in Calcium (Milk, Eggs) and expose the body to morning sunshine (Vitamin D).

}, {image: assets/science/musklo-skeletal-system/quest_14_bone_diseases/tuberculosis.png, title: 3. Tuberculosis (TB) of the Spine, description:

Cause: Bacteria (Mycobacterium).

Effect: It destroys the vertebrae (backbone), causing a painful hunchback (Kyphosis).

Prevention: Immunisation with BCG Vaccine at birth. Drinking boiled milk (to avoid bovine TB).

}, {image: assets/science/musklo-skeletal-system/quest_14_bone_diseases/tetanus.png, title: 4. Tetanus (Lockjaw), description:

Cause: Bacteria (Clostridium tetani) found in soil.

Entry: Enters the body through fresh cuts or wounds (especially from rusty metal).

Signs: Stiff muscles, difficulty breathing, and lockjaw.

Prevention: DPT Vaccine. Cover wounds. Use sterilized tools.
}]}
